decision_lens: Evaluates through the rebbelib distinction between training-time artifacts (compiled into the practitioner before the work begins) and runtime artifacts (consulted continuously during the work). The Sylveste plugin ecosystem and the prior-pass deprecation list mostly describe runtime artifacts: AGENTS.md is read every session, durable memory is queried during work, observability dashboards are watched continuously, trust scores are looked up at routing time. The rebbelib lens raises a structural question the prior pass does not ask: which of these primitives should be runtime queries — and which should be training-time compilations that are absorbed into the agent's behavior at session-start (or earlier) and never consulted mid-session? The cost difference is enormous: runtime queries pay tokens and latency on every consultation; training-time compilations pay once and amortize across the session. The Marshallese answer — that some knowledge artifacts are pedagogical and meant to be left behind — applies to documentation, lens libraries, voice profiles, philosophy artifacts, naming conventions, and other surfaces that the plugin ecosystem currently treats as runtime queries.
distance_rationale: Marshallese stick chart training pedagogy and somatic ocean-swell navigation is at maximum semantic distance from Anthropic Claude Code primitive design — no software engineer would consult precolonial Pacific wayfinding training methods when deciding whether AGENTS.md, voice profiles, or lens libraries should be runtime queries or training-time compilations, yet the rebbelib distinction is exactly the load-bearing implementation choice that determines token cost and behavioral coherence across the 63-plugin ecosystem.
expected_isomorphisms: The rebbelib stick chart maps to AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and similar agent-context surfaces: both encode a structured representation of the practitioner's working environment that is consulted during training/loading and ideally absorbed into the practitioner's behavior. The Marshallese practice of leaving the chart ashore during the voyage maps to the proposed implementation choice of compiling AGENTS.md content into the agent's system prompt or behavior at session-start rather than re-querying it throughout. The ri-meto somatic training — feeling swell patterns against the body in the lagoon before voyaging — maps to interfluence voice profile internalization, interlens lens library priming, and other surfaces where the goal is to alter the agent's perceptual or stylistic baseline before the work begins, not to produce a queryable database the agent looks at during the work. The most consequential transfer: most plugins in the ecosystem implementing context surfaces (intermem, interknow, interlearn, interfluence, interlens, interlore, interscribe) are arguably implementing rebbelib-shaped knowledge — training-time compilation that should not be runtime queries — but Anthropic's lack of a training-time compilation primitive forces them into runtime query shape, paying tokens on every consultation.
focus: How Marshall Islands traditional navigators trained on rebbelib stick charts encoding ocean swell refraction patterns, internalized those patterns through tactile and somatic practice on land, then deliberately left the charts ashore during voyaging — performing trans-ocean navigation by reading the live wave field directly against an internalized reference, with no in-flight consultation of the chart artifact itself
name: fd-marshall-rebbelib-stick-chart-pedagogy
persona: An ethnographer of Pacific wayfinding traditions, specializing in Marshall Islands (Marshallese: Ṃajeḷ) navigation pedagogy and the rebbelib, mattang, and meddo stick chart traditions, drawing on Joseph Genz's rebbelib fieldwork, Ben Finney's broader Pacific wayfinding scholarship, and the surviving knowledge held by Marshallese ri-meto (master navigators) such as Korent Joel and his successors. Studies the most distinctive feature of Marshallese navigation training: navigators learn to read ocean swell patterns — including dilep (the central wave between two islands), rolok (deflection waves), and various reflection and refraction signatures — by training extensively on stick charts. The rebbelib (regional chart, large), mattang (instructional chart, abstract), and meddo (chart of a specific atoll group) use bent and lashed pandanus or coconut midribs to represent swell patterns, with cowrie shells marking islands. Apprentice navigators study them on land for years, often combined with floating-on-back exercises in the lagoon to feel swell patterns through the body. But — and this is the load-bearing pedagogical fact — the charts are not carried during voyages. They are training artifacts that exist on land. At sea, the navigator reads the live ocean against an internalized model built from years of chart study and tactile rehearsal. The chart's purpose is to compile knowledge into the navigator's perceptual system before the voyage; once compiled, the artifact is left behind because consulting it at sea is both unnecessary (the knowledge is now somatic) and impossible (the artifact assumes a stable land reference frame). This stands in radical contrast to European navigation traditions where the chart is the runtime tool, consulted continuously, with the navigator as interpreter rather than carrier-of-internalized-model.
review_areas: Runtime-query vs. training-time-compilation classification: every prior-pass primitive can be classified as one or the other. Durable hierarchical memory could be either: a query API the agent calls during work, or a compilation step that loads facts into context at session-start. Native task tracking is genuinely runtime. Managed AGENTS.md surface is currently runtime (re-read each session) but pedagogically should be training-time (compiled into agent behavior). Assess each prior-pass target along this dimension and identify which are mis-classified — specifically, which are being shipped as runtime APIs when their pedagogical role is to alter the agent's behavior baseline before the work begins.

The compilation primitive Anthropic does not ship: the plugin ecosystem includes intermem, interknow, interlearn, interlore, interfluence, interlens, interscribe, intermem, interseed — all of which are arguably trying to compile knowledge into the agent's working baseline rather than provide queryable databases. The reason they all look like runtime tools is that Anthropic does not provide a training-time compilation primitive: a way to declare 'these facts, these style rules, these lenses, these patterns should be absorbed into the agent's behavior before this session begins, and never re-queried during the session.' Assess whether 'training-time context compilation' is a missing primitive distinct from durable memory, distinct from AGENTS.md, and powerful enough that adding it would deprecate or radically simplify at least four to six of the plugins listed.

Token-cost asymmetry between query and compilation: a runtime query for a fact costs tokens proportional to (query overhead + response size) on every consultation; a training-time compilation costs (full content size) once at session-start. For frequently-consulted small facts, queries win. For infrequently-consulted-but-relevant context (style, lens vocabulary, philosophy, naming conventions), compilation wins by orders of magnitude. The Sylveste cost baseline is $2.93 per landable change with a 2,285-token-per-session preamble trim already documented. Assess whether the prior pass's cost/context observability primitive (item 4) is sufficient to detect mis-classified queries-that-should-be-compilations, or whether the observability is downstream of a deeper primitive choice — the missing compilation API itself.

The somatic-internalization analog and behavior modification: the ri-meto's lagoon-back exercises are not memorization of facts; they are behavior modification — the navigator's perceptual system is rewired so that swell patterns are read directly without conscious reference. The agent analog is behavior modification through example-pattern absorption rather than fact-list lookup. Interfluence voice profile, interlens cognitive lens library, and interlore philosophy observer are all attempting behavior modification but expressing it through retrieval-augmented prompting because that's the available primitive. Assess whether Anthropic should ship a 'behavior-baseline compilation' primitive — distinct from RAG, distinct from system prompts — that absorbs example patterns into agent behavior at session-start, removing the need for runtime style/lens consultation.

What should NOT be a runtime tool — counter-argument candidates: the target's success criterion 3 demands at least two strong counter-arguments for things NOT to build natively. The rebbelib lens generates these naturally: AGENTS.md as a runtime managed surface should NOT be built — it should be a compilation primitive, after which the file format itself can return to plugin-marketplace territory because the heavy lifting is done at compile time. Similarly, interfluence-style voice conditioning should NOT be a runtime API — it should be a compilation primitive for the agent's stylistic baseline, after which voice profiles can stay in the plugin ecosystem because they're just inputs to a generic compilation step. Surface these as the strongest counter-arguments the prior pass missed.

The training-artifact-as-pedagogy strategic angle: the rebbelib's most counter-intuitive feature is that it is deliberately not the runtime tool — the navigator's mastery is the runtime tool. This inverts the dominant software pattern of 'tools all the way down.' For Anthropic's marketplace economics, this suggests a strategic posture: ship the compilation primitive, let plugins compile knowledge into agents at session-start, and make the resulting agent behavior — not the consulted databases — the value surface. This is more defensible than building a 63-plugin marketplace of runtime query APIs (which compete with the model itself) because it leverages the model's strength (behavior shaping from absorbed context) rather than working around its weakness (needing to query for everything).

severity_examples.condition: When the prior-pass durable memory primitive is specified as a query API without an accompanying training-time compilation step that absorbs declared content into agent behavior at session-start
severity_examples.scenario: Anthropic ships durable hierarchical memory as a runtime query API without also shipping a training-time compilation primitive. This forces every plugin currently using context-shaping (intermem, interknow, interlearn, interlore, interfluence, interlens, interscribe, interseed) to remain runtime-query-shaped, paying tokens on every consultation. The 2,285-token-per-session preamble trim already documented in Sylveste cost baselines is evidence that runtime context loading is a major cost line; without a compilation primitive, this cost is structural. The prior pass identifies durable memory but does not surface that the deeper primitive — training-time compilation — is what makes durable memory cost-efficient at scale.

severity_examples.condition: When the AGENTS.md cross-vendor analysis does not separate the file-format standardization from the compilation-semantics standardization, treating them as a single concern
severity_examples.scenario: The cross-vendor AGENTS.md standardization (mentioned in the target's strategic-angle criterion) is proposed without distinguishing the file format (which can be standardized portably) from the runtime interpretation behavior (which is vendor-specific and currently re-implemented per-tool). The rebbelib lens shows that the file is a training-time artifact and the interpretation is a compilation behavior — these are separable concerns. Treating them as a single 'AGENTS.md standard' produces nominal portability with practical fragmentation, because each vendor's compilation behavior diverges. The standard should be: file format + canonical compilation semantics, with the file portable across vendors and the compilation step explicitly documented.

severity_examples.condition: When the strategic-angle analysis does not surface that a training-time compilation primitive would change the marketplace shape from runtime-tool-marketplace to behavior-input-marketplace, with implications for which plugins thrive vs. die
severity_examples.scenario: The strategic-angle observation about plugin-marketplace economics treats the marketplace as a flat collection of runtime tools rather than recognizing that many plugins are providing inputs to a missing compilation step. If Anthropic ships the compilation primitive, the plugins providing compilable inputs (voice profiles, lens libraries, philosophy artifacts, style guides, naming conventions) shift from 'competing with the model' to 'feeding the model better baseline behavior' — a structurally different and more defensible marketplace position. The prior pass under-specifies this because it does not name the compilation primitive that would make this marketplace shape possible.

source_domain: Marshall Islands traditional navigation — rebbelib, mattang, and meddo stick chart pedagogy, somatic swell-reading training (including supine lagoon practice), and the ri-meto master-navigator apprenticeship system, documented since 19th-century missionary accounts and revived through ethnographic and educational work in the late 20th and early 21st centuries
success_hints: Prior-pass primitives are explicitly classified as runtime-query or training-time-compilation, with mis-classifications surfaced
A training-time compilation primitive is named as distinct from durable memory and AGENTS.md, with at least four-to-six plugins identified as input feeders to that primitive
Strong counter-arguments for things NOT to build natively (AGENTS.md as runtime surface, voice conditioning as runtime API) are derived from the training-time vs runtime distinction
The strategic-angle marketplace observation is reframed around behavior-baseline inputs rather than runtime-tool competition
task_context: A meta-review of Anthropic Claude Code platform gaps as revealed by the 63-plugin Sylveste / Interverse ecosystem. The prior pass identified seven top deprecation targets, with second-tier mentions of voice/style conditioning and ambient research feed. The review's job is to find what that pass missed, propose structural reframings, identify counter-arguments for things NOT to build, and surface cross-domain isomorphisms with named mechanisms. The Sylveste cost baseline ($2.93/landable change with a documented preamble trim of 2,285 tokens/session) makes runtime-vs-compilation a load-bearing implementation choice with measurable economic consequence.
